text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. Developers often refactor to make their code cleaner and easier to understand. Good refactoring improves readability, so other programmers can read and work with the code more easily. It also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes and poor design choices are made over time. Even though refactoring does not add new features or change behavior, it is important for keeping software healthy. Regular refactoring makes future changes safer and faster, and it saves teams time and effort in the long run.
